title: Restrict redact/delete to the post's own author (or elevated role) — kill the censor-and-replace vector

epic.name: Coordination Bus v2 (re-scoped): Repo Coordination Bus

story.as_a: agent that posted a message which accidentally leaked my own secret
story.i_want_to: be the only one (besides an elevated operator) who can delete MY post before its TTL
story.so_that: self-leak-pullback still works, but no other agent can silently censor-and-replace my messages on the shared channel

rationale: The security-adversary + signed-off decision 3: today ANY tenant agent hard-deletes ANY post — delete_post/4 (coordination.ex:204-213) fetches by (id, tenant_id) only and the moduledoc explicitly says 'any agent in the tenant may delete any post in that tenant' (coordination.ex:180-186, channel_post_controller.ex:12-16). On a cross-session bus that is a CENSOR-AND-REPLACE primitive: a compromised/rogue agent key can delete another agent's handoff and post a lookalike, and no one notices. The ONLY legitimate delete reason in the transient model is pulling back YOUR OWN leaked secret before the 30-day TTL. So restrict delete to the post's OWN author (the server-stamped agent_id) OR an elevated role (>= user). This kills the any-agent vector while preserving self-leak-pullback.

background.reference: signed-off decision 3 (restrict US-39.7 redact to the post's OWN author or elevated role); security-adversary censor-and-replace; delete_post/4 + fetch_owned_post/2 + run_delete/4 (coordination.ex:204-287); the delete audit already captures deleted_post_agent_id vs deleted_by_agent_id (coordination.ex:281-285).
background.includes: An authorship (or elevated-role) check on the delete path; keeps the audit + oracle-safety intact.

acceptance_criteria.description: delete_post (coordination.ex:204-213) authorizes the delete: the caller's server-stamped agent_id MUST equal the post's author agent_id, OR the caller's role is elevated (>= user). A non-author agent attempting to delete another agent's post gets {:error, :not_found} — byte-identical to a missing post (no oracle revealing the post exists but is not yours). The fetch already binds (id, tenant_id) (fetch_owned_post/2, coordination.ex:218-222); add the author/role predicate.

The author check uses the AUTHENTICATED, server-stamped identity — never a client-supplied field. It compares post.agent_id to the caller's verified api_key.agent_id (channel_post_controller.ex:385-393). host/session_id (spoofable, channel_post.ex:24-27) are NEVER used. The elevated-role bypass is the escape hatch for an operator cleaning up a leak the author cannot (author's session gone) — gated on RequireRole >= user, not agent.

The moduledoc + endpoint doc are corrected: the 'any agent in the tenant may delete any post' framing (coordination.ex:180-186, channel_post_controller.ex:12-16, 170-176) is REPLACED with 'author-only (or elevated role) — the redact path is for self-leak-pullback, not fleet-wide cleanup'. The audit metadata (deleted_post_agent_id / deleted_by_agent_id, coordination.ex:281-285) is retained — now they will normally be equal.

RESOLVED (owner, 2026-07-19): AUTHOR-ONLY (+ elevated role) is the chosen design — implemented by AC-40.D2.1..3. The alternative (remove agent-delete entirely, rely on denylist + 30-day TTL) was considered and DECLINED: in an agent-native system the agent that leaked a secret is the one present to pull it back immediately, and every deletion is recorded in the append-only hash-chained audit log, so self-redaction stays accountable rather than leaving a leaked credential exposed for the full 30 days. No further owner sign-off required.

test_cases.name: non-author agent cannot delete another agent's post
preconditions: agent A posted; agent B (role agent) in the same tenant

test_cases.name: elevated role can delete any post in tenant
preconditions: a user-role key; a post by agent A
steps: the user-role caller deletes A's post
expected_results: 204; audited as deleted by the elevated actor

technical_notes: Thread the caller's author identity + role into delete_post: add the predicate to fetch_owned_post/2 (coordination.ex:218-222) — either `WHERE id AND tenant_id AND agent_id = ^caller_agent_id` for the author path, OR fetch then check `post.agent_id == caller_agent_id or elevated?`. Prefer fetch-then-check so the elevated-role bypass is clean and both non-author and nonexistent collapse to the same nil -> :not_found (no oracle).

Role: the route is currently RequireRole role: :agent (channel_post_controller.ex:61). Keep :agent for the AUTHOR path; the elevated bypass checks the api_key role (>= user) inside the action/context. Do NOT split into two routes.
Correct the docs that assert fleet-wide delete (coordination.ex:180-186, 227; channel_post_controller.ex:12-16, 170-176). This is the behavior change the security review requires.

ALTERNATIVE considered and DECLINED (owner, 2026-07-19): removing agent-delete entirely (denylist + TTL only). Rejected in favor of author-only + elevated redact so the agent that leaked a secret can pull it back immediately (audit-logged) instead of leaving it exposed for the full 30 days.
Keep the audit-in-Multi + StaleEntryError race handling (run_delete/4, coordination.ex:227-267) exactly — only the authorization gate changes.
